harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured 512MB zstd-compressed zram swap on node1 via an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node2), verified it activates automatically at boot with priority 100 (preferred over any disk-backed swap), and completed the mandatory single-node-at-a-time restart/recovery protocol for both node1 and node2.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Ubuntu 24.04, no existing swap) and node2 (ansible-core 2.20.5 pre-installed, confirming it as the control node)

Fixed a pre-existing broken sshd on node1 (missing host keys, service crash-looping) so the control node could reach it, and wired up passwordless SSH from node2 to node1 using the cluster-provided keypair

Playbook installs linux-modules-extra-<kernel> (zram.ko was missing from the base linux-modules package), installs systemd-zram-generator, loads/persists the zram module, writes /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf (zram-size=512, compression-algorithm=zstd, swap-priority=100), lowers priority of any disk-backed fstab swap, starts/enables dev-zram0.swap, and verifies via swapon --show
Ran the playbook (first run failed on missing zram module, fixed the role, re-ran to success), then re-ran again to confirm full idempotency (changed=0)
Verified live: /dev/zram0 512M swap active, priority 100, comp_algorithm shows [zstd] selected, disksize=536870912 bytes (512MiB)

Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, service/ansible state) for node1 and node2, restarted node1 via systemd reboot (ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and that zram swap came back automatically with zero manual steps, reconfirmed via Ansible ad-hoc from node2
Repeated the same baseline/restart/verify cycle for node2 (the control node), confirming Ansible, SSH, and the playbook files all survived and node1's zram swap remained healthy throughout

evidence.requirement: Ansible-based 512MB compressed zram swap configured on node1, active and preferred
evidence.summary: Playbook (using systemd-zram-generator with zram-size=512, compression-algorithm=zstd, swap-priority=100) applied successfully; live check shows /dev/zram0 512M swap active at priority 100 with zstd selected as the compression algorithm and no disk-backed swap present to compete with it
Second playbook run reports changed=0 across all 12 tasks
Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-... and confirmed zram swap healthy via the playbook's verify task just before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll failed with connection reset (node down); later poll returned new boot_id 88a33921-... proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered state and swap active-at-boot proof
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: /dev/zram0 512M swap active at priority 100 with zstd compression came up automatically with no manual intervention; SSH and Ansible ad-hoc command from node2 both confirm the swap state

evidence.requirement: node2 (control node) healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id c030bd0d-..., confirmed ansible-core functional and playbook files present, ssh socket listening

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll returned new boot_id 4ad94106-..., proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: node2 recovered state (control-node functionality) after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: ansible-core operational, playbook/inventory files intact, and an Ansible ad-hoc command against node1 successfully confirms node1's zram swap is still active — proving the control path fully recovered
